judged_text: The server schema (guests: z.array(z.string().email()), lines 3-6) omits the uniqueness refinement its client twin applies (AddGuestsDialog.tsx lines 28-31), and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-78) only removes duplicates against already-stored attendees, never within the input array itself. A request containing the same email twice (['a@x.com','a@x.com']) passes server validation and createMany persists two Attendee rows for one person on one booking — duplicating them in the attendee list, the ICS, and email dispatch — or fails with an unhandled Prisma P2002 500 where a (bookingId, email) unique constraint exists; either outcome breaks the uniqueness guarantee the endpoint's own error message promises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the client-side dialog enforces unique emails via a zod `.refine` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) but the server input schema only validates email format (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts) and the handler’s `uniqueGuests` filter only excludes emails already present on the booking and blacklisted ones (addGuests.handler.ts), not duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. As written, an input like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] is accepted by the server and will be passed to `createMany` as duplicated data, causing duplicated attendees or a DB error depending on constraints (not shown in the diff). Either way, it violates the endpoint’s implied uniqueness guarantee and can break downstream attendee lists / calendar update / emails.
